subject: ventures/workers-comp-premium-calculator
professional: a commercial-lines workers' compensation underwriter or premium auditor (or an insurance broker's account manager for contractors), who checks first that the NCCI Basic Manual order of operations is followed (manual premium, experience mod, schedule rating, premium discount, then non-discountable constants and surcharges), that the overtime exclusion matches the audit rule, and that the final-audit true-up uses the same rates on actual payroll

evidence.correctness: Ran node --test calc.test.mjs page.test.mjs usage.test.mjs from the venture dir: 27 tests, 27 pass, 0 fail. Recomputed policyPremium() independently in a separate Python script from the NCCI Basic Manual premium sequence (payroll/100 x rate; x experience mod; x (1 + schedule%); less premium discount; plus surcharge; plus expense constant): (1) class A $200,000 payroll incl. $30,000 overtime at 1.5x, rate 8.50, class B $50,000 rate 0.45, mod 1.15, schedule +10%, discount 5%, surcharge 2%, expense constant 250, fees 100: OT exclusion 30,000 x 0.5/1.5 = 10,000, basis 190,000, manual 16,150 + 225 = 16,375, modified 18,831.25, scheduled 20,714.375, discount 1,035.72, after-discount 19,678.66, surcharge 393.57, total 20,422.23; the tool printed 16375 / 18831.25 / 20714.38 / 1035.72 / 19678.66 / 393.57 / 20422.23 (identical to the cent). (2) auditTrueUp: estimated $100,000, actual $130,000, rate 5, mod 0.90: expected +30,000/100 x 5 x 0.9 = 1,350 additional; tool: 1350 'additional'. (3) reclassImpact(100000, 8.5, 3.2, 0.9) expected 1000 x (3.2 - 8.5) x 0.9 = -4,770; tool -4770; overtimeExclusion(30000, 2.0) expected 15,000; tool 15000; modSensitivity at $100k, rate 5: 0.10 of mod = $500, tool up 500 / down 500 / per001 50. Ran, not just read. Limits: the premium discount is a single user-typed percentage, so the NCCI tiered discount table (applied to standard premium by size band) is not computed; the user must work it out themselves.
evidence.completeness: Checked each README feature by calling it: overtimeExclusion, classPremium, policyPremium, modSensitivity, auditTrueUp, reclassImpact and findings all exist and return what the README says; index.html imports policyPremium, modSensitivity, auditTrueUp, reclassImpact, findings and usage.mjs, and has a Calculate button, audit true-up input, usage opt-out and a skipped-items list. README 'Tests' claims no-network assertions: page.test.mjs exists. No TODOs or stubs found. VENTURE.yaml stage is 'prototype' and both hypotheses are untested. Gaps a user would meet: no printable or savable result, no premium discount table, no minimum-premium check. I did not load the page in a browser; completeness of the in-page wiring rests on source reading and page.test.mjs.
evidence.verification: node --test calc.test.mjs page.test.mjs usage.test.mjs: 27 pass, 0 fail. Seeded five mutations in calc.mjs one at a time, ran calc.test.mjs (10 tests), reverted with git checkout (git status clean for the venture dir afterwards). (A) overtime exclusion divisor m -> 2: caught (3 fail). (B) premium discount base scheduled -> modified (discount taken on the pre-schedule amount): NOT caught, 10/10 pass. (C) findings dominant-class threshold 0.6 -> 0.7: NOT caught. (D) flat-charges finding threshold 0.15 -> 0.25: NOT caught. (E) schedule-rating cap max 25 -> 35: NOT caught. The core arithmetic of manual premium, overtime and audit direction is pinned, but the order of the discount/schedule steps, which changes the dollar total, is not, and validation limits and finding thresholds are untested at their boundaries. Page tests are regex checks over HTML source; nothing executes the inline script.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (all 140 lines), calc.test.mjs, README.md, VENTURE.yaml, robots.txt, sitemap.xml, llms.txt and the index.html head, script imports and disclaimer sections. Pure ES-module functions, no dependencies, a single num() validator that throws on missing, non-numeric or out-of-range input instead of clamping (matches the claim), cents() rounding at each step with fixed order. Defects: per-step rounding to cents means totals can differ by a cent from a carrier that rounds only at the end; the findings() sort/threshold magic numbers are unexplained; `rel=canonical href=./index.html`, sitemap.xml `<loc>./index.html</loc>` and robots.txt `Sitemap: ./sitemap.xml` are relative URLs that search engines reject; schedulePct limits (+/-25) are applied to every state although the permitted range is a state rule; `(step * 100 || 1)` in modSensitivity is a silent fallback that hides a zero step. No dead code of note.
evidence.claims: Disclaimer present and repeated: page line 112 'Not insurance, legal, tax, or financial advice. Your carrier's quote and audit control.', FAQ 'Is this an insurance quote?', and a 'No warranty' footer paragraph; README 'Limits'. Checked claims against files: 'entirely client-side, nothing uploaded' -> index.html has no fetch/XMLHttpRequest, imports only ./calc.mjs and ./usage.mjs (backed); 'no rate table ships' -> calc.mjs has none (backed); 'out-of-range inputs throw instead of being clamped' -> num() throws (backed); 'overtime exclusion (m-1)/m' -> overtimeExclusion (backed, and recomputed). Weaknesses: README 'Tests' says `node --test ventures/workers-comp-premium-calculator/` which VENTURE-level guidance and Node 22 reject (repo requires `node --test '*.test.mjs'`), so the documented command does not work as written; llms.txt links the superseded duncan-haywood.github.io address rather than the live https://marisstella.app/workers-comp-premium-calculator/ named in README and VENTURE.yaml; README claims 'hand-counted figures for every step' but the discount-after-schedule ordering is not pinned (mutation B); canonical, sitemap and robots URLs are relative so the SEO claim in VENTURE.yaml is not backed in practice; the README 'After using this you can now...' sentence is promotional with no measured users (stage prototype, hypotheses untested).
evidence.fitness: Walked a landscaping contractor with a renewal quote: types 2 class payrolls and rates from the declarations page, mod 1.15, a schedule debit, discount, constants; gets a line-by-line rebuild, a dollar value for 0.10 of mod, and an audit true-up when actual payroll is entered. That does the stated job and matches the quote when the carrier's discount percentage is typed in. Gaps in the first hour: the owner usually does not have the premium-discount percentage (carriers compute it from a size table), so the total will not tie to the quote unless they back it out; terrorism, catastrophe and state assessments (normally part of standard premium and discountable) must be entered as the single 'surcharges' percentage applied after discount, which can be the wrong order; no per-class mod or split-rate handling; no minimum-premium or owner-officer payroll limit; no way to save or print. Usage is unmeasured, so real-world fitness is untested.
evidence.domain: Compared against the NCCI Basic Manual / experience-rating plan order of operations and standard-premium practice: manual premium = payroll/100 x rate; experience mod multiplies manual premium; schedule rating applies to the modified premium; premium discount applies to standard premium (the discountable portion) and the expense constant is added after discount, not discounted. The tool's order (manual, mod, schedule, discount, surcharges, expense constant and fees) matches the common practice, and the (m-1)/m overtime exclusion, the 0.3 to 3.0 mod range and the audit true-up using the same rates are accepted practice. Departures a premium auditor would flag: (1) the discount is a flat typed percentage rather than the tiered size-band table; (2) the surcharge percentage is applied after discount, but terrorism and catastrophe charges are usually in standard premium and some assessments are not discountable, so the ordering depends on the line item and is not explained; (3) overtime exclusion is not universal (some states and monopolistic funds differ) and the page says 'most states, check yours' (honest); (4) the schedule +/-25% cap is state-specific, not universal; (5) experience mod is user-typed with no split-point or ownership-change handling, which is disclosed. Acceptable as a premium-reconciliation worksheet, not as a quote replacement.

defects.what: Premium-discount base is not pinned by tests: changing it from the scheduled premium to the modified (pre-schedule) premium leaves all 10 calc tests passing, although it changes the dollar total whenever a schedule debit or credit is entered together with a discount.

Premium discount is a single user-typed percentage and surcharges are applied after discount; owners rarely hold the discount percentage, so the total will not tie to a real quote without outside work, and terrorism/catastrophe charges (part of standard premium) are in the wrong place if entered as 'surcharges'.
README documents `node --test ventures/workers-comp-premium-calculator/` as the test command; the repository's Node 22 convention rejects a bare directory and needs '*.test.mjs' from the venture dir.
canonical link, sitemap loc and robots Sitemap line use relative URLs, which search engines do not accept; llms.txt links the superseded duncan-haywood.github.io address instead of marisstella.app.

Validation limits (schedule +/-25, discount 0 to 30, mod 0.3 to 3) and findings thresholds (0.6 dominant class, 0.15 flat charges) are untested at their boundaries; mutations to the schedule cap and both thresholds all passed.
Rounding to cents at every step can differ by a cent from a carrier that rounds once; modSensitivity hides a zero step with `|| 1`.

verdict: A small, correct premium-reconciliation worksheet: the manual-to-total sequence, overtime exclusion, audit true-up, reclass and mod sensitivity all reproduced to the cent against an independent recomputation, the disclaimer is strong and repeated, and the no-upload and no-rate-table claims are backed by files. It does not meet the bar because verification scores 2 and claims 2: four of five seeded mutations survived the tests (including swapping the base the premium discount is taken on, which changes dollars), the README's test command does not work as written under the repository's Node convention, and the SEO URLs (canonical, sitemap, robots, llms.txt) are relative or point at a superseded host. Domain and fitness stay at 2 because the premium discount is a typed percentage rather than the size-band table and surcharges are applied after discount, so the total will not tie to a real quote without hand adjustment. Cheap fixes: a test with schedule debit plus discount pinning the order, boundary tests for the validation limits, correct the README test command, absolute URLs in canonical, sitemap, robots and llms.txt.
